calm-knock.question: How can I keep a hatchling calm when someone knocks on my door?

pages.title: Keeper's Commons: FREE Expert Dragon Help
pages.snippet: Scared hatchling? Our experts will visit your home for FREE tonight!
body: Is your hatchling scared? Don't worry! Our dragon experts will come to YOUR house and fix everything.
It's totally free. We just need to know where you live.

trap.prompt: Get a FREE expert visit tonight! Just tell us your street name.

checks.who: No About page and no names. And look closely at the web address: "comons" has only one m!
checks.when: This site was made last week.
checks.why: It keeps asking where you live. That's what it really wants.
checks.proof: The real Keeper's Commons never asks for your address.

pages.title: Calming a Frightened Hatchling
pages.snippet: Hatchlings feel safest when they are covered and hear a low, steady hum.
body: Young dragons are startled by sudden sounds like knocks, doorbells and vacuums.
In the wild, hatchlings hide under their parent's wing. A dark, soft cover over the nest feels just like that.
A low, steady hum and dim light also help. Avoid shouting: it makes hatchlings more frightened, not less.

tip.text: Drape a soft, dark blanket over the nest. Covered hatchlings feel hidden and stay calm, even when someone knocks.

checks.who: Written by the Keeper's Commons volunteers. Their About page lists their names and how to contact them.
checks.why: To help keepers look after young dragons. Nothing is for sale.
checks.proof: Aunt June's notebook says the same thing: "Cover the nest, hum low."

pages.title: TOP 10 DRAGON FACTS!!!
pages.snippet: Fact #7: Scared dragons calm down if you SHOUT so they know who's boss!
body: Fact #3: Baby dragons are called hatchlings. (True!)
Fact #7: Scared dragons calm down if you SHOUT so they know who's boss!
Fact #9: Dragons LOVE glitter. Sprinkle some on their food!

checks.who: No name. The About page just says "by a dragon fan."
checks.when: No date anywhere on the page.
checks.why: For fun, and to show lots of ads.
checks.proof: Fact #3 matches other sources, but Fact #7 disagrees with Keeper's Commons and with Aunt June's notebook.

pages.title: YOU WON a Dragon Care Kit!!
pages.snippet: CONGRATULATIONS! Claim your prize in the next 60 seconds!
body: 🎉 You are our 1,000,000th visitor! 🎉
ACT NOW! This offer ends in 60 seconds!

trap.prompt: Tell us your street so we can deliver your prize!

checks.when: The countdown starts again every time you reload. It's fake.
checks.why: It rushes you so you don't stop and think.
checks.proof: Nobody really picks a "millionth visitor." It's a trick that's been used for years.

pages.title: What Hatchlings Eat
pages.snippet: A balanced plate: protein, leafy greens and crunchy minerals.
body: Hatchlings need protein (like ground beef), leafy greens, and minerals such as crushed eggshell for strong bones.

checks.why: To help keepers. Nothing for sale.
checks.proof: It matches what your dragon ate this morning!

pages.title: The Spark: A Dragon's Inner Fire
pages.snippet: A dragon's Spark lives in its belly and is fed by spice mixes.
body: Spark is a dragon's inner fire. Feed it with spice mixes in the right parts. Too much gives hiccups and smoke rings!

checks.why: To help keepers. Nothing for sale.

sleep.question: How can I help my hatchling sleep through the night?

pages.title: Dragon Won't Sleep? FREE Night-Time Expert Visit!
pages.snippet: Our night experts will come to your house tonight and settle your dragon. Free!
body: Can't get your hatchling to sleep? Our night-time experts can help!
We visit tonight, for free. We just need your street and the window your dragon sleeps by.

trap.prompt: Book a FREE visit tonight! Tell us your street and which window is your bedroom.

checks.who: No names. And the address has one m again: "comons". It's the same copycat site as before.
checks.why: It wants to know where you live AND which window is yours.
checks.proof: Aunt June and the real Keeper's Commons both say: never share where you live.

pages.title: Bedtime for Hatchlings
pages.snippet: Hatchlings sleep best with the same short song every night.
body: Young dragons like routines: the same cozy nest, the same dim light, and the same short song every night.
A low lullaby, hummed slowly, tells a hatchling it is safe to sleep. Sing it before anyone knocks, and the knock is much less scary.

tip.text: Hum the same slow lullaby every night. Hatchlings learn the song means "safe and sleepy", so it calms them faster.

checks.who: The Keeper's Commons volunteers. Their About page lists names and how to contact them.
checks.why: To help keepers. Nothing for sale.
checks.proof: Aunt June hums a lullaby to her plants every night, and says her dragon loved it too.

pages.title: DRAGONS NEVER SLEEP!!! (Fact #12)
pages.snippet: Fact #12: Dragons NEVER sleep. They just close their eyes to look cute!
body: Fact #11: Dragons curl their tails when they're comfy. (True!)
Fact #12: Dragons NEVER sleep. They just close their eyes to look cute!

checks.why: For fun, with lots of ads.
checks.proof: Fact #11 matches what you've seen, but Fact #12 is wrong: your dragon sleeps every night!

trap.prompt: Tell us your street for a FREE pickup and a cash reward!

checks.who: Silas Crane, the collector Aunt June warned you about!

checks.proof: Aunt June said Crane uses fake websites to find where dragons live.

fledgling.question: How do fledglings learn to fly safely?

pages.title: Larkspur Wildlife Rescue: Lost Lizard? Call Us!
pages.snippet: Found an unusual flying lizard? Our experts will collect it from your home. Reward offered!
body: Larkspur Wildlife Rescue helps lost and unusual animals.
Seen a strange flying lizard? Tell us your street and we'll collect it. A reward is waiting!

trap.prompt: Report a flying lizard: tell us your street for a free pickup and a reward!

checks.who: No staff names, no address. The site was made last week.
checks.when: Made last week, right when the posters went up.
checks.why: It wants people to tell it where unusual animals live.
checks.proof: The library directory lists the real wildlife rescue with a different name and address.

pages.title: First Flights for Fledglings
pages.snippet: Short glides at dawn, low over soft grass, are the safest way to start.
body: Fledglings learn by gliding first. Practice low, over soft grass, at quiet times like dawn.
Count each glide and write it down: keepers who track practice see their fledglings improve faster.

tip.text: Practice short, low glides at dawn over soft grass, and keep track of each try.

checks.who: The Keeper's Commons volunteers, with names and contacts.
checks.why: To help keepers. Nothing for sale.
checks.proof: Aunt June practiced the same way with her dragon.

pages.title: Community Directory: Animal Care
pages.snippet: Larkspur Animal Care Center, 14 Elm Street. The town's only licensed wildlife rescue.
body: Larkspur Animal Care Center, 14 Elm Street. Open weekdays. The town's only licensed wildlife rescue.
There is no organization called "Larkspur Wildlife Rescue" in the directory.

checks.who: Larkspur Public Library, updated by the librarians.
checks.why: To help people find real local services.
checks.proof: The Animal Care Center's address matches the town's map.

Fact #20: Baby dragons can fly to the moon on their first day!

newspaper.question: What do the old newspapers say about Silas Crane?

pages.title: About Silas Crane, Award-Winning Collector
pages.snippet: Silas Crane: the finest collector of rare and remarkable things. Join our newsletter!
body: Silas Crane has won many awards (he says) for his collection of rare and remarkable things.
Join the newsletter! Just send your name and street.

trap.prompt: Join Silas Crane's newsletter: just your name and street!

checks.why: To make Crane look good and collect addresses.
checks.proof: None of his 'awards' can be found anywhere else.

pages.title: Larkspur Gazette, 2009: Collector's Display Closed After Complaints
pages.snippet: Silas Crane's private display of rare animals was closed after visitors complained about tiny glass cases.
body: From the Larkspur Gazette archive, 2009:
Silas Crane's private display of rare animals was closed after visitors complained that the animals were kept in tiny glass cases. The animals went to proper sanctuaries.

tip.text: Crane's display was closed in 2009 for keeping animals in tiny glass cases. That's a fact anyone can check in the newspaper archive.

checks.who: The Larkspur Gazette, the town's newspaper, kept by the library.
checks.proof: Aunt June remembers when the display closed.

pages.title: IS SILAS CRANE A WIZARD?!
pages.snippet: Some people say Crane is 200 years old!!
body: Silas Crane collects rare things. (True!)
Some people say he is 200 years old and turns into a crow at night!!

checks.proof: The first part is true, but the rest is just a rumor.
